habitat: Bornean orangutans inhabit the lowland tropical rainforests, peat swamp forests, and mountain forests of Borneo at elevations up to 1,500 meters. They are found in both the Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak and the Indonesian province of Kalimantan. Their preferred habitat includes primary dipterocarp forests with abundant fruit trees and old-growth forest with tall, sturdy trees for nesting. Deforestation for palm oil and logging has dramatically reduced their habitat.
diet: Bornean orangutans are primarily frugivorous, with fruit making up 60-90% of their diet depending on season. They show remarkable dietary flexibility, consuming over 400 different food items including leaves, bark, flowers, honey, insects, and occasionally bird eggs. During fruit-scarce periods, they rely on 'fallback foods' like bark and leaves. They play an essential ecological role as seed dispersers, spreading seeds throughout the forest through their feces.
behavior: Bornean orangutans are the most arboreal of the great apes, spending 90% or more of their time in trees. They are largely solitary, with the only lasting bond being between mother and infant. Females give birth once every 6-8 years — the longest interbirth interval of any land mammal. Each night, they build a new sleeping nest from branches and leaves. They are highly intelligent, using tools in the wild including sticks for extracting insects and leaves as umbrellas.
facts: Orangutans share 97% of their DNA with humans. The word 'orangutan' means 'person of the forest' in Malay. Bornean orangutans are distinguished from Sumatran orangutans by their broader faces, shorter beards, and darker red-brown coloration. There are three subspecies of Bornean orangutan. They can live up to 45 years in the wild and over 50 in captivity. They are critically endangered, with an estimated 55,000 remaining.
naming: Bornean-inspired names for pets or characters might reflect their arboreal nature and red coat. Consider names like Borneo, Kalimantan, Hutan (forest), Api (fire), Ember (for their reddish hair), Canopy, Forest, Rusty, Copper, Mahogany, or Megah (magnificent in Malay).
